selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why does the note say some ideas from other books of the Risale-i Nur appear again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because those other parts were not present where this work was written, so important points from them were included here too.

questions.question: Did the note present the repeated material as pointless, or as necessary for a reason?
questions.answer: It presents it as necessary for a clear reason.

questions.question: How should a reader understand this overlap according to the note?
questions.answer: The reader should see it as understandable repetition caused by circumstances, not as careless writing.

questions.question: Why were the students told to copy the present treatise anyway?
questions.answer: So they could have a short version that still contained the whole Risale-i Nur in essence.

questions.question: What is notable about the person who copied the revised version?
questions.answer: He is praised as blessed even though he was not trained in such subjects.

questions.question: What exact feature of the writing was counted?
questions.answer: The alifs appearing at the beginning of the lines were counted.

questions.question: Which title is connected with that numerical match?
questions.answer: The title is Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: According to the note, what did the number show about the title The Supreme Sign?
questions.answer: It showed that the title was especially fitting for the treatise.

questions.question: What significance did the count of 666 have?
questions.answer: It matched the abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What problem in the writing process made the treatise include material also found elsewhere in the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: The other relevant books were unavailable in the place where this treatise had to be written.

questions.question: Because of that absence, what happened in this treatise?
questions.answer: Important points from The Words and The Flashes were also included in it.

questions.question: What phrase in the note shows that the writing of this treatise could not be delayed?
questions.answer: It says the treatise had to be written there out of necessity.

questions.question: What makes the pattern in that copy seem remarkable?
questions.answer: It seems remarkable because the copyist was not informed about such symbolic details.

questions.question: How many alifs were counted, and why was that number important?
questions.answer: There were 666, and that number matched the numerical value of the treatise’s title in the abjad system.

questions.question: What was counted in relation to that letter?
questions.answer: The number of alifs placed at the beginnings of the lines was counted.

questions.question: What does the note say was missing at the place where the treatise was composed?
questions.answer: Other sections of the Risale-i Nur were missing there.

questions.question: After the rough version, who prepared the revised copy?
questions.answer: A blessed person prepared it.

questions.question: What special pattern was noticed in his copy?
questions.answer: The beginnings of the lines contained a precise number of alifs.

questions.question: What exact number was found in that pattern?
questions.answer: The number found was 666.

questions.question: What letter is central to the pattern mentioned?
questions.answer: The letter alif.

questions.question: What is said about the person who wrote the revised copy?
questions.answer: He is described as a blessed person, even though he did not know much about these matters.

questions.question: Where in the writing did this pattern appear?
questions.answer: It appeared in the alifs at the starts of the lines.

questions.question: Even so, what was discovered in the copy he produced?
questions.answer: A delicate and meaningful letter pattern was discovered in it.

questions.question: What does the note say about the revised copy’s writer in terms of his knowledge?
questions.answer: It says he lacked expertise in these subjects.
